title: Tame trait quotient and change of logarithmic base
statement:
A trait is $\operatorname{Spec}R$ for a Noetherian local domain of dimension one with principal maximal ideal. It is complete strictly henselian if $R$ is complete for that ideal, is henselian (simple roots of monic polynomials over its residue field lift), and has separably closed residue field. Its canonical log structure is $\mathcal O\cap j_*\mathcal O_\eta^\times$, where $j$ includes its generic point. Mixed characteristic means fraction-field characteristic zero and positive residue characteristic.

Let $S^{\prime}\to S$ be a finite dominant extension of complete strictly henselian mixed-characteristic traits. Let a finite group $H$ act on $S^{\prime}$ over $S$, with $\#H$ invertible on $S$. Put $R^{\prime}=\Gamma(S^{\prime},\mathcal O_{S^{\prime}})$ and $T=\operatorname{Spec}((R^{\prime})^H)$, where $(R^{\prime})^H=\{r:h(r)=r\text{ for all }h\in H\}$. Then $T$ is a complete strictly henselian trait, $T\to S$ is finite dominant, and $S^{\prime}\to T$ is finite dominant and log etale for the canonical fs log structures [def-per-fs-log-smooth-etale, def-trf-fs-log-blowup]. Its generic-field degree divides $\#H$, allowing a nonfaithful action. For every locally Noetherian fs log scheme $V$ log smooth over $S^{\prime}$, the composite $V\to T$ is log smooth. Here finite means affine with module-finite coordinate algebras [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and dominant means having dense image.

proof.text: Translate finiteness of Spec(R -> B) to module finiteness. Dense spectrum image implies the kernel lies in the nilradical, hence is zero because R is a domain. The fixed subalgebra A embeds R-linearly into the finite R-module B, so Noetherian submodule finiteness makes A finite over R, and therefore Noetherian. The same R-generators make B finite over A. Thus both displayed spectrum maps are finite. Injectivity of R -> A follows by its composite into B; A -> B is the subtype inclusion. Their kernels are zero, so both spectrum maps have dense image.

Dimension one excludes R and B being fields. The Noetherian-local-domain DVR equivalences turn their principal maximal ideals into DVR instances. Apply the algebraic tame-invariant Kummer presentation to obtain A a strictly henselian DVR, n>0 dividing |H| with generic degree n and n invertible, uniformizers pi,tau, and the specified evaluation equivalence. A nonfield PID has Krull dimension one and principal maximal ideal. Independently apply the finite-over-complete-local product theorem to the finite R-algebra A: as a domain it is complete for its maximal ideal. Proof irrelevance identifies its local-ring structure with the strictly henselian one.

Apply the general divisorial rank-one Kummer realization to A,B,n,pi,tau and the evaluation equivalence. It supplies the canonical fs log structures and the log-etale quotient map over the actual inclusion. Retain its structural identifications and underlying-map equation. Substitute degree=n into n divides |H|. Log etale implies log smooth; compose any log-smooth V -> SB with q by the existing composition theorem, retaining its full CompEq section-map equation. Assemble the conjunction.
